title: Calm, practical directions
question: Four quiet options. Each comp shows the AI import review over Downtown Cinema 7.

options.label: Booking Sheet
options.thesis: Warm paper-white, graphite type, hairline rules; the review reads like a tidy booking form you sign off line by line.
options.viewport: Full-width review grouped Updates / New / Archive / Skipped, one ruled row per change, sticky apply bar.
options.risk: So quiet it can feel plain; craft has to live in spacing and type.

options.label: Projection Booth
options.lineage: a booth at night, low light
options.thesis: Soft charcoal, off-white type, one warm amber only for what still needs your approval.
options.viewport: Schedule on the left, the review as a wide right panel; pending items carry a thin amber rule.
options.risk: Dark product UIs drift toward generic dev-tool dark mode.

options.label: Timetable
options.thesis: White and black with one quiet blue reserved for what the AI proposed; old values struck through inline.
options.viewport: Changes grouped by auditorium like a timetable, strike-and-blue diffs inline, archives listed at the end.
options.risk: Grouping by auditorium splits a film's showtimes across sections.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Linear / Vercel / Stripe-dashboard console, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, filters over a table, the review as a right side sheet.
